comment: Model A permits the HUID to be “derived from” the national identifier. Derivation can expose or make the national identifier predictable and may conflict with the later requirement for a non-intelligent identifier.

anchor.note: p.117 l.Lines 131-134 read as the printed page; section 4 agrees

public.text: Model A permits the HUID to be “derived from” the national identifier. Derivation can expose or make the national identifier predictable and may conflict with the later requirement for a non-intelligent identifier.
public.suggestedRevision: Prefer a random health identifier linked to, rather than derived from, foundational identifiers. If derivation is permitted, require a privacy and security justification and prohibit reversible or meaningful encoding.
